records.name: Consistency
records.summary: A sequence of estimators converges in probability to the target parameter for every parameter value.
records.statistical_question_answered: Does the estimator become accurate with large samples?
assumptions_required: Estimator sequence and target are specified.
conditions_required: Convergence in probability holds under each θ.
does_not_guarantee: It does not guarantee unbiasedness or good small-sample performance.
use_when: MLE asymptotics, method comparisons, simulation planning.
do_not_use_when: Small samples or nonregular models without finite-sample checks.
common_misuses: Using consistency as if it guarantees accuracy at n=20.
diagnostic_questions: How large is n and what convergence rate is known?

records.name: Limiting variance
records.summary: A scaled limiting value of the estimator variance.
records.statistical_question_answered: How does estimator variability scale with n?
assumptions_required: Estimator sequence and scaling constants are specified.
conditions_required: Scaled variance has a finite limit.
does_not_guarantee: It does not necessarily equal variance of a limiting distribution in all cases.
do_not_use_when: When convergence distribution or scaling is unknown.
common_misuses: Mixing up finite-sample variance, limiting variance, and asymptotic variance.
diagnostic_questions: What scaling is used?

records.name: Asymptotic variance
records.summary: The variance parameter in a scaled limiting normal distribution.
records.statistical_question_answered: What variance appears in the limiting law?
records.problem_addressed: Enables approximate standard errors and intervals.
assumptions_required: A scaled estimator has a limiting normal distribution.
does_not_guarantee: It does not ensure finite-sample normality.
do_not_use_when: Small samples or nonnormal limiting laws.
common_misuses: Using asymptotic SE as exact SE.
diagnostic_questions: What is the limiting distribution?
checks_or_evidence_needed: Delta method, Fisher information, or simulation.

records.name: Asymptotic efficiency
records.summary: An estimator sequence reaches the Cramer-Rao lower bound in its asymptotic variance.
records.statistical_question_answered: Is the estimator first-order optimally precise in large samples?
records.decision_improved: Improves selection among consistent asymptotically normal estimators.
conditions_required: Asymptotic normality and CRLB conditions hold.
does_not_guarantee: It does not imply robustness or finite-sample optimality.
use_when: MLE comparisons in regular parametric models.
common_misuses: Choosing an estimator solely by asymptotic efficiency.
diagnostic_questions: Are regularity conditions plausible?

records.name: Asymptotic relative efficiency
records.summary: A ratio of asymptotic variances comparing two asymptotically normal estimators.
records.statistical_question_answered: Which estimator has smaller large-sample variance?
records.problem_addressed: Provides a scale-free comparison of asymptotic precision.
assumptions_required: Both estimators target the same parameter and share √n limiting normal scale.
conditions_required: Asymptotic variances are finite and positive.
does_not_guarantee: It does not compare bias, robustness, or small-sample behavior unless reflected in limit variance.
use_when: Mean versus median, robust estimator comparisons.
do_not_use_when: Different targets, rates, or nonnormal limits.
common_misuses: Comparing AREs when estimators have different assumptions.
diagnostic_questions: Do both estimators have the same target and rate?

records.name: Breakdown value
records.summary: A robustness measure describing how much extreme contamination can occur before a statistic becomes unbounded.
records.statistical_question_answered: How resistant is a statistic to extreme outliers?
records.decision_improved: Improves estimator choice under contamination risk.
assumptions_required: Ordered sample and statistic are specified.
guarantees: Resistance to catastrophic outliers is quantified.
does_not_guarantee: It does not describe efficiency under ideal normality.
use_when: Mean versus median and robust estimator discussion.
do_not_use_when: When the main issue is model bias rather than outliers.
common_misuses: Assuming robust means efficient or unbiased.
diagnostic_questions: How many extreme points can ruin the statistic?

records.plain_language_meaning: Under regularity conditions, MLEs and continuous functions of them are consistent.
records.conclusion: MLEs have large-sample convergence to the true parameter/function.
records.why_it_matters: Supports large-sample use of likelihood estimators while requiring regularity checks.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Use likelihood concentration around the true parameter and continuity of τ.
common_misuse: Assuming every numerical maximizer is consistent
what_breaks_if_assumptions_fail: Nonidentifiability, boundary, or misspecification can break consistency.

records.plain_language_meaning: Under stronger regularity conditions, continuous functions of MLEs are asymptotically normal and attain the Cramer-Rao bound.
records.formal_statement_shape: √n[τ(θ̂)-τ(θ)] →d N(0, v(θ)) where v is CRLB.
records.conclusion: MLEs are first-order asymptotically efficient in regular models.
records.why_it_matters: Justifies large-sample standard errors and Wald intervals.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Expand score/log-likelihood around true θ and use information identities plus delta method.
common_misuse: Applying under irregular models, small n, or boundary parameters
what_breaks_if_assumptions_fail: Asymptotic normal calibration may be unreliable.

records.result_name: Asymptotic distribution of LRT, simple null
records.plain_language_meaning: For a regular one-parameter test of a simple null against two-sided alternative, -2 log likelihood ratio converges to chi-square with one degree of freedom.
records.conclusion: LRTs can be calibrated approximately by chi-square distributions in large samples.
records.why_it_matters: This reduces need for exact null distributions in many regular problems.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Use Taylor expansion of log-likelihood around the MLE/null and asymptotic normality of the MLE/score.
common_misuse: Using chi-square LRT calibration in nonregular cases
what_breaks_if_assumptions_fail: Type I error can be badly wrong.

records.result_name: Asymptotic chi-square LRT for nested composite nulls
records.plain_language_meaning: Under regularity, -2 log likelihood ratio converges to chi-square with degrees of freedom equal to difference in free parameter dimensions.
assumptions: Random sample from regular parametric model.
Nested null with regular parameter restrictions.
conditions: Random sample from regular parametric model.
Nested null with regular parameter restrictions.
records.conclusion: Composite LRTs get a general large-sample reference distribution.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Approximate log-likelihood quadratically around constrained and unconstrained MLEs.

what_breaks_if_assumptions_fail: The limiting distribution may not be chi-square with naive df.
